About.title: About
About.overview: GymSpot is a digital platform that connects gyms, coaches, and clients in one ecosystem designed to simplify hiring, marketing, and communication in the fitness industry.
About.forGymsDescription: GymSpot acts as both a recruitment and marketing platform. Gyms can publish job posts for coaching positions, allowing qualified coaches to apply directly. At the same time, gyms can promote their business by showcasing their profiles, including photos, available plans, and location.
About.forCoachesDescription: GymSpot creates career opportunities and personal branding. Coaches can discover job openings and apply directly. In addition, coaches can market themselves by offering online coaching services, highlighting certifications and transformation results.
About.searchDiscoveryDescription: Our advanced search system allows users to browse gyms and coaches with filters such as location, city, or name, making it easy to find the right fit.
About.communicationDescription: Built-in private chat and real-time notifications ensure seamless interaction between gyms and coaches without leaving the platform.
About.aiFeaturesDescription: GymSpot integrates AI to enhance your experience. Our AI assistant helps you understand job posts, coaches, gyms, and applicants better.
About.summaryDescription: Combining recruitment, marketing, communication, and intelligence into one powerful platform for the fitness world.

Exercises.title: Train by
Exercises.description: Tap any muscle on the body to discover simple, effective exercises you can start today — then connect with a coach to build your full plan.
Exercises.hint: Tap a muscle to see exercises
Exercises.emptyState: Pick a muscle group to get started.
Exercises.ctaDesc: Find a certified coach to perfect your form and plan.

shoulders.name: Shoulders
shoulders.focus: Build round, capped delts for a wider frame.

exercises.name: Overhead Press
exercises.tip: Press the bar straight up, keep your core tight.
exercises.description: Stand tall with the bar at shoulder height. Press straight overhead until your arms lock out, then lower under control to the front of your shoulders.
exercises.failureTip: Choose a weight you can press for 8 clean reps. On the final set keep pressing until you can't lock out a rep with good form — that is true failure.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise
exercises.tip: Raise to shoulder height, lead with the elbows.
exercises.description: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Raise them out to the sides up to shoulder height with a slight bend in the elbows, then lower slowly.
exercises.failureTip: Use a light weight and high reps. Keep raising until your side delts burn and you can't reach shoulder height, then squeeze out 2-3 partial reps.

exercises.name: Front Raise
exercises.tip: Lift to eye level, no swinging.
exercises.description: Hold the weight in front of your thighs. Lift it forward and up to eye level with straight arms, then lower with control. No swinging or leaning back.
exercises.failureTip: Go until you can't raise the weight to eye level without using momentum. Stop the set the moment your form breaks.

exercises.name: Bench Press
exercises.tip: Lower to mid-chest, drive up through your feet.
exercises.description: Lie on the bench, grip slightly wider than your shoulders. Lower the bar to mid-chest, then drive it back up while keeping your feet planted and back stable.
exercises.failureTip: Always train heavy chest with a spotter. Push until you can't lock out a rep, then let the spotter help you grind out the final 1-2 reps.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.tip: Targets the upper chest, controlled tempo.
exercises.description: Set the bench to about 30 degrees. Press the dumbbells up and together over your upper chest, then lower slowly until you feel a stretch.
exercises.failureTip: On your last set, lower the dumbbells slowly (3 seconds) and keep pressing until you can't fully extend your arms anymore.

exercises.name: Push-ups
exercises.tip: Keep a straight line from head to heels.
exercises.description: Hands under your shoulders, body in a straight line. Lower your chest to the floor, then push back up while keeping your core braced.
exercises.failureTip: Do as many strict reps as you can. When you can't complete another full rep, drop to your knees and squeeze out a few more to hit failure.

biceps.name: Biceps
biceps.focus: Add size and a strong peak to your arms.

exercises.name: Barbell Curl
exercises.tip: Keep elbows pinned to your sides.
exercises.description: Hold the bar with an underhand grip. Curl it up by bending only at the elbows, squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to a full stretch.
exercises.failureTip: When you can't curl another clean rep, do a couple of 'cheat' reps with a tiny swing, then lower super slowly — this pushes the muscle safely past failure.

exercises.name: Hammer Curl
exercises.tip: Neutral grip hits the brachialis.
exercises.description: Hold dumbbells with palms facing each other. Curl up keeping the neutral grip, then lower with control. Great for overall arm thickness.
exercises.failureTip: Reach failure on one arm, then the other, then finish with a few slow negatives where you fight the weight on the way down.

exercises.name: Incline Cable Curl
exercises.tip: Keep the stretch on the biceps.
exercises.description: Sit back on an incline bench holding a low-pulley cable handle in each hand. With arms hanging back, curl up by bending only at the elbows, squeeze hard, then lower under full control to a deep stretch.
exercises.failureTip: On the last set curl until you stall, then let the cable pull your arms into a slow stretch and grind out a few partial reps at the bottom.

forearms.name: Forearms
forearms.focus: Stronger grip and fuller lower arms.

exercises.name: Reverse Curl
exercises.tip: Overhand grip, slow and steady.
exercises.description: Hold the bar with an overhand grip. Curl it up keeping your wrists firm, then lower slowly. Builds the top of the forearm and grip strength.
exercises.failureTip: Use a weight that's hard by rep 10. Push until your grip starts to fail, then squeeze out 2-3 partial reps.

exercises.name: Farmer's Walk
exercises.tip: Carry heavy, walk tall.
exercises.description: Pick up a heavy dumbbell in each hand, stand tall, and walk with controlled steps. Brilliant for grip, forearms and overall toughness.
exercises.failureTip: Walk until your grip gives out and you have to set the weights down — that grip failure is exactly the point of the exercise.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.tip: Brace your abs, don't let your hips sag.
exercises.description: Rest on your forearms and toes, body in a straight line. Squeeze your abs and glutes and hold without letting your hips drop or rise.
exercises.failureTip: Hold until your form breaks and your hips start to sag — that shaking is your core reaching failure. Note the time and beat it next session.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.tip: Lift your legs with control, no swinging.
exercises.description: Hang from a bar. Keeping your legs fairly straight, raise them up toward parallel using your lower abs, then lower slowly without swinging.
exercises.failureTip: When you can't lift your legs to parallel anymore, switch to bent-knee raises and keep going until your abs give out.

exercises.name: Crunches
exercises.tip: Curl your ribs toward your hips.
exercises.description: Lie on your back, knees bent. Curl your shoulders off the floor by contracting your abs, pause at the top, then lower slowly.
exercises.failureTip: Do slow reps with a 1-second squeeze at the top until you can't curl up anymore, then finish with short partial crunches.

quads.name: Quads
quads.focus: Powerful thighs and a solid base.

exercises.name: Squat
exercises.tip: Sit back, knees tracking over your toes.
exercises.description: Bar on your upper back, feet shoulder-width. Sit back and down until your thighs are about parallel, then drive up through your heels.
exercises.failureTip: Squat heavy only inside a rack with safety pins. Push until you can't stand a rep up, then set it on the pins — never grind to collapse without safeties.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.tip: Full range, don't lock your knees.
exercises.description: Sit in the machine, feet shoulder-width on the platform. Lower until your knees reach about 90 degrees, then press back without locking out.
exercises.failureTip: Leg press is the safest way to train legs to true failure — keep pressing until your quads can't extend the platform, then do a few partial reps.

exercises.name: Lunges
exercises.tip: Step long, drop the back knee.
exercises.description: Step forward into a long stride, lower your back knee toward the floor, then push back to standing. Alternate legs each rep.
exercises.failureTip: Keep lunging until your legs are burning and your balance starts to go, then finish the set with bodyweight-only reps.

traps.name: Traps
traps.focus: Build a thick, strong upper back.

exercises.name: Shrugs
exercises.tip: Lift your shoulders to your ears, hold a second.
exercises.description: Hold a heavy weight at your sides. Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears, hold the squeeze for a second, then lower slowly.
exercises.failureTip: Use a heavy load and keep shrugging until you can barely lift your shoulders, then hold a hard squeeze at the top for 15-20 seconds.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.tip: Pull toward your forehead and squeeze.
exercises.description: Using a rope on a high pulley, pull the handles toward your forehead while spreading them apart and squeezing your upper back.
exercises.failureTip: Use light weight and chase the burn — keep pulling and squeezing until your rear delts and traps can't hold the contraction.

back.name: Back
back.focus: Wider lats and a stronger pull.

exercises.name: Pull-ups
exercises.tip: Pull your chest up to the bar.
exercises.description: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip. Pull your chest up toward the bar by driving your elbows down, then lower under full control.
exercises.failureTip: Do strict reps to failure, then use a small jump or a band to keep doing assisted reps and slow negatives past your limit.

exercises.name: Bent-over Row
exercises.tip: Flat back, pull to your waist.
exercises.description: Hinge forward with a flat back, holding the bar. Pull it to your lower stomach by squeezing your back, then lower under control.
exercises.failureTip: When you can't pull the bar all the way to your waist, allow a tiny bit of body english and keep rowing partial reps to finish the set.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.tip: Drive your elbows down and back.
exercises.description: Grip the bar wider than your shoulders. Pull it down to your upper chest by driving your elbows down, then let it rise slowly to a full stretch.
exercises.failureTip: Keep pulling until you can't bring the bar to your chest, then drop the weight a little (drop set) and immediately rep out again.

triceps.name: Triceps
triceps.focus: Fill out the back of your arms.

exercises.name: Triceps Dips
exercises.tip: Lower until your elbows hit 90 degrees.
exercises.description: Support yourself on parallel bars or a bench. Lower your body by bending your elbows to about 90 degrees, then press back up to lockout.
exercises.failureTip: When you can't press back up from the bottom, use your legs (on a bench) to assist slightly and keep going with slow negatives.

exercises.name: Rope Pushdown
exercises.tip: Lock your elbows, extend fully.
exercises.description: Using a rope on a high pulley, keep your elbows pinned and push the rope down, spreading the ends apart at the bottom. Return slowly.
exercises.failureTip: Pin your elbows and push until you can't fully straighten your arms, then do partial reps at the bottom until the triceps are fully spent.

exercises.name: Overhead Extension
exercises.tip: Keep your elbows close to your head.
exercises.description: Hold a dumbbell overhead with both hands. Lower it behind your head by bending the elbows, then extend back up, keeping your elbows tucked.
exercises.failureTip: Lower slowly for a deep stretch and keep extending until you can't lock out — the stretch position is where the triceps fail first.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.tip: Squeeze your glutes hard at the top.
exercises.description: Upper back on a bench, bar across your hips. Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body is flat, squeezing hard at the top.
exercises.failureTip: Hold a hard squeeze at the top of every rep and keep thrusting until your glutes can't fully lock out, then pulse a few partials at the top.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.tip: Hinge at the hips with soft knees.
exercises.description: Hold the bar in front of your thighs. Push your hips back and lower the bar along your legs until you feel a glute/hamstring stretch, then stand tall.
exercises.failureTip: Stop the set when your lower back can no longer stay flat — protecting your spine matters more than chasing a few extra reps here.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.tip: Drive through your heels.
exercises.description: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat. Lift your hips toward the ceiling by squeezing your glutes, then lower slowly.
exercises.failureTip: Add a weight on your hips and rep out until you can't fully raise them, then finish with a long 20-30 second hold at the top.

exercises.name: Leg Curl
exercises.tip: Curl slowly, squeeze the back of the thigh.
exercises.description: Lie or sit in the machine. Curl the pad toward you by bending your knees, squeeze the hamstrings hard, then lower slowly under control.
exercises.failureTip: Curl until you can't bring the pad all the way in, then fight the negative slowly on each remaining rep until the hamstrings give out.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.tip: Feel the stretch, keep the bar close.
exercises.description: Hinge at the hips and lower the bar down the front of your legs until you feel a deep hamstring stretch, then drive your hips forward to stand.
exercises.failureTip: Push until you can't keep a flat back — never round your spine for extra reps. The loaded stretch is what drives growth, not grinding.

calves.name: Calves
calves.focus: Complete your legs with strong calves.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.tip: Rise up high, pause at the top.
exercises.description: Stand with the balls of your feet on a step. Rise up as high as you can onto your toes, pause, then lower your heels for a deep stretch.
exercises.failureTip: Calves are stubborn — keep raising until you can't rise onto your toes anymore, then do slow partial reps and a long stretch at the bottom.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.tip: Slow stretch at the bottom.
exercises.description: Sit with the weight on your knees and the balls of your feet on the platform. Raise your heels as high as possible, then lower slowly into a stretch.
exercises.failureTip: Use a 2-second squeeze at the top and a 2-second stretch at the bottom, and keep going until your calves can't lift the weight at all.

exercises.name: Jump Rope
exercises.tip: Light, quick bounces on the balls of your feet.
exercises.description: Bounce lightly on the balls of your feet, turning the rope with your wrists. A great calf endurance and conditioning finisher.
exercises.failureTip: Jump continuously until your calves are too fatigued to keep a steady rhythm — that burning fatigue is the goal for endurance failure.
